evidence.claim: TikTok says it collects information you provide, automatically collected information, and information from other sources.
TikTok says some advertisers and partners integrate TikTok Advertiser Tools (such as TikTok Pixel) that let TikTok collect similar information from their websites or apps.
TikTok says it uses information to provide and improve advertising services and measure the effectiveness of ads it serves.
Cookies can be refused or disabled in device browser settings, which may control some information collected.
In-app settings let you update account information, request a copy of your data, or deactivate or delete your account.

TikTok says advertisers and partners can integrate its Advertiser Tools to let it collect information from their sites and apps, and offers in-app settings to request your data or delete your account.

Exodus Privacy static analysis of version 36.5.4 (report dated Sept. 17, 2024) found code signatures for 7 known tracker SDK(s): AppsFlyer (analytics), Facebook Analytics (analytics), Facebook Login (identification), Facebook Share, Google Firebase Analytics (analytics), IAB Open Measurement (identification advertisement), Pangle (advertisement). A signature shows the SDK is present, not what data it sends.

Version 36.5.4 lists these sensitive Android permissions in its manifest: advertising ID, approximate location, audio files, camera, contacts, microphone, photos, read shared storage, videos, write shared storage (Exodus Privacy, Sept. 17, 2024); a declared permission does not show the data is collected or how it is used.
